title: 500 Venezuela migrants living in Colombia block a highway in protest of the lockdown due to the COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia. They say the makes it impossible for them to work. There are 1.8 million Venezuelan migrants living in Colombia.
text: The COVID-19 pandemic in Colombia was a part of the pandemic of coronavirus disease 2019 caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS-CoV-2). The virus was confirmed to have reached Colombia on 6 March 2020.

title: The United States Army sends a Security Force Assistance Brigade unit to Colombia to train anti-drug forces for a period of four months.
text: A Security Force Assistance Brigade (pronounced ESS-fab) is a specialized United States Army unit formed to conduct security force assistance (SFA) missions: to train, advise, assist, enable and accompany operations with allied and partner state armed forces. title: A soldier, Ángel Zúñiga Galicia, removes his uniform and puts down his gun in refusal of an order to remove peasants from their home in Pance, Valle del Cauca Department.
text: Valle del Cauca is a department in western Colombia abutting the Pacific Ocean. Its capital is Santiago de Cali.

title: Seven soldiers confess to raping a 12-year-old girl from the Embera Katio indigenous group, in the northwestern Risaralda Department.
text: Catío Emberá is an indigenous American language spoken by the Embera people of Colombia and Panama. The language was spoken by 15,000 people in Colombia, and a few dozen in Panama, according to data published in 1992.

title: Colombia requests the extradition of drug lord and paramilitary warlord Salvatore Mancuso, 56, on fears that he may be deported to Italy and released. Mancuso has been convicted over 1,000 murders and other crimes.
text: Salvatore Mancuso Gómez, also known as "el Mono Mancuso", "Santander Lozada" or "Triple Cero", among other names (born August 17, 1964) is a Colombian paramilitary leader, once second in command of the United Self-Defense Forces of Colombia (AUC) paramilitary group.

title: Two thousand indigenous Arhuaco protest against armed groups who are seizing land in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta.
text: The Arhuaco are an Indigenous people of Colombia. They are Chibchan-speaking people and descendants of the Tairona culture, concentrated in northern Colombia in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta.

title: Three miners are rescued after being trapped for five days by a cave-in in Lenguazaque, Cundinamarca Department.
text: Cundinamarca is a department of Colombia. Its area covers 22,623 square kilometres (8,735 sq mi) (not including the Capital District) and it has a population of 2,919,060 as of 2018 (3,445,300, DANE 2023 projections).

title: The Climate Green Fund of the United Nations donates US$28 million to prevent deforestation in the Amazon rainforest.
text: The Amazon rainforest, also called the Amazon jungle, Amazonia, or simply the Amazon, is a moist broadleaf tropical rainforest in the Amazon biome that covers most of the Amazon basin of South America. This basin encompasses 7 million km2, of which 6 million km2 (2.3 million sq mi) are covered by the rainforest.

title: Opening of La Línea road tunnel.
text: La Línea is a highway tunnel between the cities of Calarcá, Quindío and Cajamarca, Tolima in Colombia. It crosses beneath the locally famous "Alto de La Línea" in the Cordillera Central or central range of the Andes mountains, easing traffic on one of Colombia's main east-west road connections (the National Route 40) which links Bogotá with Cali and the Pacific port of Buenaventura.

title: A statue of Spanish conquistador Sebastián de Belalcázar is torn down by indigenous Misak in Popayán, Cauca Department in protest of 500 years of slavery and oppression.
text: Sebastián Moyano y Cabrera, best known as Sebastián de Belalcázar was a Spanish conquistador.

title: The telenovela Amar y vivir premiers on Colombian television.
text: Amar y vivir is a Colombian telenovela produced by Fox Telecolombia that premiered on 7 January 2020 on Caracol Televisión, and ended on 14 April 2020. The series is created by Nubia Barreto based on the 1988 telenovela of the same name written by Germán Escallón and Carlos Duplat.
